fetch_url.description: Fetch a URL and return its real content, not a summary. Returns JSON verbatim, article pages as clean markdown, YouTube links as transcripts, and PDFs/images downloaded to a local path.

mode.description: auto by default; article, raw, and json force extraction modes

where_is.description: Get someone's current live location via Find My. person defaults to the owner themselves; pass a phone/email for someone sharing location with them.

person.description: phone/email to locate; omit for the owner themselves

watch_arrival.description: Ping the owner when they reach a place. Give the destination as a name or address; when their live location comes within radius_m of it, they get note as a text.
watch_arrival.notes: File-backed local watch; eventual outbound text is handled by harness.

note.description: the message to text on arrival

cancel_arrival_watch.description: Cancel an arrival watch by id.

set_reminder.description: Set a reminder. when is an absolute ISO datetime. text is the short message the owner should receive when it fires.

text.description: the message to send when it fires

recall_conversations.description: Search the full iMessage history with the owner (every message ever) and get back ranked snippets — not whole messages. This is the ONLY way to search Conversations/ — grepping the folder is blocked by the harness, because a grep there returns entire messages and one common word can blow 60k+ tokens of context. (Reading one specific dated transcript end-to-end is still fine and sometimes right.) Search is HYBRID — keyword matching fused with semantic similarity — so you do NOT have to guess the owner's exact words. Asking in your own phrasing works: 'the guy from apple nyc' finds the message naming them. Plain natural-language questions are fine and often better than keyword soup. "Quoted phrases" still match exactly when you do know the wording. Optional: speaker ('sam' or 'fig') to search only one side, since/until as YYYY-MM-DD, limit (default 15, max 50). Results are best-match-first, «guillemets» around a keyword hit. Snippets are windows — if you need the full message, the date+time in each result tells you which line of Conversations/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md to read.

query.description: what you're looking for — a natural-language question or keywords, both work

speaker.description: only search one side of the conversation

schedule_task.description: Schedule a one-off full agent task for a future time. Unlike a reminder, this runs a future agent pass with prompt. when is an absolute ISO datetime.
schedule_task.notes: Schedules future harness work; no immediate external action.

prompt.description: what the future agent pass should do

maxLateMinutes.description: drop without running if more than this many minutes late (default 60)

list_scheduled_tasks.description: List pending one-off scheduled agent tasks.

cancel_scheduled_task.description: Cancel a scheduled agent task by id.

jobs_list.description: List all async background jobs: running and recently finished.
jobs_list.notes: Main-process job registry; stdio fallback runtimes run out-of-process.

jobs_check.description: Check one background job by id. Finished jobs are marked as seen to avoid duplicate push delivery.
jobs_check.notes: Main-process job registry; stdio fallback runtimes run out-of-process.

id.description: job id, e.g. browse-3 or codex-1

jobs_cancel.description: Cancel/kill a running background job by id. Does not launch new work.
jobs_cancel.notes: Main-process job registry; stdio fallback runtimes run out-of-process.

agentmail_check_inbox.description: List recent messages in one of fig's AgentMail inboxes. Defaults to fig's persistent address. Returns message_id values for agentmail_read_message.

address.description: inbox address; omit for fig's persistent address

agentmail_read_message.description: Open one full AgentMail message. Defaults to fig's persistent address when address is omitted.

address.description: inbox address; omit for fig's persistent address

govee_lights.description: Control the owner's Govee lights (their physical smart lights) — turn on/off, set color, brightness, or white temperature, or read their state. Lights: 'Monitor Light Bars' + 'TV Light Bars' and 2x 'Smart LED Bulb'. target is a name substring (e.g. 'bulb', 'tv', 'monitor') or 'all' (default). For action=color, value is a color name / #hex / 'r,g,b'. For action=brightness, value is 1-100. For action=temp, value is Kelvin 2000-9000.
govee_lights.notes: controls the owner's own home lights

target.description: light name substring or 'all'; defaults to 'all'

value.description: color (name/#hex/'r,g,b') for color; number for brightness (1-100) or temp (Kelvin)

web_export.description: Pull the owner's data out of a website via its web-export adapter (a local per-site exporter at ~/GitHub/web-export). source is the adapter name (e.g. 'x-bookmarks', 'canvas'), or 'list' to see which sources exist. maxPages optionally caps how many pages to page through. On success returns the path to the written JSON file; on failure returns the CLI's error text — most commonly a missing one-time session capture that has to be grabbed from a logged-in browser tab before that source can run.
web_export.notes: Shells out to the local web-export CLI to pull data from a site; some sources need a one-time session capture on disk first.

source.description: adapter name to export (e.g. 'x-bookmarks', 'canvas'), or 'list' to see available sources

maxPages.description: optional cap on pages to pull (maps to --max-pages=N); omit to pull everything
